rule: Lua: module = the name the scan's `require` strings give the file (`core.common` for data/core/common.lua; ambiguous matches go to the require root that explains the most requires ...). Functions on the module's returned table are `mod#fn`
notes: Each `require` is an invocation of the loader: `_G#require`, medium, direct, on its line (Decisions 2026-11-10, CommonJS / Lua `require`). main.lua is not itself required; it sits at the require root (src/) that explains every require string in the case, so the name a require from that root gives it is `main` (Lua note: 'module = the name the scan's `require` strings give the file'). call_type convention (SPEC lists the types but gives no Lua mapping): a `:` call is method, a `.` or bare call is direct (the 2026-11-10 require ruling makes `_G#require` direct), a call through a value is callback. The require strings name core/init.lua `core` (`require "core"` loads `?/init.lua` through package.path's `./?/init.lua` template, Lua 5.2+ default and lite-xl's path), not `core.init`. So its returned-table functions are `core#start` / `core#loop`, reached from its own file and from view.lua and main.lua (C1). core/view.lua is required as "core.view": `core.view#draw`, and its top-level require has caller `core.view`.
